summary: Defines a BGP opaque extended community that carries the origin validation state within an autonomous system, so IBGP speakers can use it in local policy.

eli5.summary: A tag marking whether a route's origin was checked, passed to neighbors inside a network.

questions: what is the bgp origin validation state extended community
what do origin validation state values mean in bgp
should ebgp peers accept the origin validation community
how does ibgp share rpki validation results
subtitle: A BGP tag that passes a route's origin validation result between routers inside one network.

tldr.problem: A router can check whether a route's origin AS is valid, but other routers in the same autonomous system may not be able to do that check themselves.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 8097 defines an opaque BGP extended community whose last octet carries the validation state: 0 for valid, 1 for not found, 2 for invalid. Routers attach it on IBGP sessions.
tldr.outcome: Receiving IBGP speakers can use the state in local policy and best-path selection. By default the community is dropped when it arrives from an EBGP peer.

today: RFC 8097 is a Proposed Standard published in March 2017. The unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Why Carry Validation State
sections.content:
RFC 8097 defines a new BGP opaque extended community that carries the origination AS validation state inside an autonomous system. Internal BGP (IBGP) speakers that receive this state can configure local policies that let it influence their decision process.

The validation state itself is the one computed by origin validation as described in RFC 6811. This document only adds a way to hand that result from one router to another.
sections.eli5: One router does the checking and writes the result on a tag. The other routers in the same network can read the tag and act on it.

sections.title: The Community Encoding
sections.content:
The community is an opaque extended community as defined in RFC 4360. It is eight octets long. The high-order octet of the extended Type field is 0x43, which indicates it is non-transitive. The low-order octet of the Type field, as assigned by IANA, is 0x00.

The Reserved fields MUST be set to 0 and are ignored on receipt. The last octet is an unsigned integer that gives the route's validation state. Three values are defined: 0 means the lookup result is valid, 1 means not found, and 2 means invalid.
sections.eli5: The tag is a small fixed-size label. Most of it is empty space, and the last piece holds a number: 0, 1 or 2, meaning good, unknown or bad.

sections.title: Sending and Receiving Rules
sections.content:
A router configured to support this extension SHOULD attach the community to BGP UPDATE messages it sends to IBGP peers, mapping its computed validation state into the last octet. A receiving BGP speaker that has no validation state set from local data SHOULD derive one from the last octet of the community, if present.

An implementation SHOULD NOT send more than one instance. If several arrive, it MUST disregard all but the one with the numerically greatest validation state value. If the value is greater than the largest specified value (2), the implementation MUST apply a strategy similar to attribute discard from RFC 7606: discard the erroneous community and log the error for further analysis.

Across AS borders the rules differ. By default, implementations MUST drop the community when it is received from an External BGP (EBGP) peer, without processing it, and SHOULD NOT send it to EBGP peers. It SHOULD be possible to configure an implementation to send or accept it when warranted, for example when two adjacent ASes are under the same administration.
sections.eli5: A router puts the tag on routes it passes to friends inside its own network. If it gets several tags, it believes the worst one. Tags from outside networks are thrown away unless the owner says otherwise.

sections.title: Deployment Considerations
sections.content: Not every speaker in an autonomous system may be upgraded to support the extension. In that case it is necessary to define policies that match on the origin validation extended community and set another BGP attribute that influences best-path selection, in the same way an implementation of this extension would. The text refers to RFC 6811 for that attribute-setting approach.
sections.eli5: If some routers in the network do not understand the tag yet, you give them a rule that turns the tag into something they do understand.

sections.title: IANA Registration
sections.content: IANA registered the value 0x00, with the name "BGP Origin Validation State Extended Community", in the "Non-Transitive Opaque Extended Community Sub-Types" registry.
sections.eli5: The official list of tag types got a new entry so nobody else uses the same number for something different.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The considerations in RFC 4272 continue to apply. Because the community will generally be used to affect route selection, the analysis of falsification in Section 4.5 of RFC 4593 is relevant. The text says these issues are neither new nor unique to this community. The security considerations of RFC 6811 apply equally.

The scheme lets router A outsource validation to router B. The participating routers should therefore have an appropriate trust relationship: B should trust A, for example because they are under the same administrative control. The security of the TCP connection between them should also be considered; see Section 5.1 of RFC 7454.
sections.eli5: If you let a friend do the checking for you, you must trust that friend and make sure nobody can whisper false answers to you on the way.
